To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Shapley-Shubik market game, a model of strategic interactions in a market, generates complex and chaotic equilibrium behavior when the number of agents is large.

(1) The equilibrium dynamics of the model are complex and chaotic for a wide range of parameter values; (2) The equilibrium dynamics can be either complex or regular depending on the values of parameters; (3) In the complex case, there is a region of parameter values for which the model exhibits chaotic dynamics; (4) The equilibrium dynamics are regular for a wide range in the parameter space.

the Shapley-Shubik market game can generate complex and chaotic equilibrium trajectories in an overlapping generations version for a broader range of preferences, in particular for a larger class of utility functions, than the perfectly competitive version.
